cards.card: Visa Ultra Cash Back Credit Card

note: Pakistan's largest banks are HBL, National Bank, UBL, MCB and Meezan; HBL and UBL, among the largest card issuers, are written; the others weren't reached in this pass. Both schedules are before federal excise duty and provincial sales tax, whose rates they don't state, and the tax isn't written. HBL's schedule of bank charges (1 July to 31 December 2026, read again 2026-10-30): service charges at most 42% a year on the amount outstanding, written at that figure, and on cash advances 42% a year; the annual fee 6,500 rupees for the HBL Green Card (this file's card since 2026-10-29), 14,000 for Gold, 22,000 for Platinum; the Fuel Saver cards a monthly fee instead, 350 rupees (Green) or 700 (Gold); a cash advance 1,200 rupees or 3%, whichever is higher; a late fee of 2,500 rupees a month; spending in another currency 4%; a returned cheque 1,200 rupees. UBL's schedule of charges (July to December 2026, effective 1 July 2026, read 2026-10-30): the Visa primary card's annual fee 6,000 rupees (Classic), 12,000 (Gold), 22,000 (Platinum); 44% a year on purchases and cash advances; a cash advance 1,200 rupees or 3%, whichever is higher; a late payment 2,200 rupees; spending abroad 4.5% or 100 rupees, whichever is higher (written as 4.5%); over the limit 1,600 rupees; a returned cheque 1,000 rupees. The Visa Signature and the Mastercards, kept for former Silkbank customers, aren't written. Neither schedule states a grace period; HBL's states no minimum payment, and UBL's does (written in wave 5). Wave 4 (2026-10-30): Bank Alfalah, a large private bank and card issuer whose schedule of charges is on its own site, is added as the third bank; MCB's and Askari's sites answer Cloudflare's block and National Bank's, Meezan's and Faysal's a 'Just a moment' check (2026-10-30). Bank Alfalah's schedule of bank charges (1 July to 31 December 2026, excluding FED and sales tax, read 2026-10-30), its credit card operations: the service charge 3.83% a month (46% APR) on the Visa Classic and 3.75% a month (45% APR) on every other card, on retail transactions and cash advances, written as monthly rates; the annual fee for the basic card: Classic 7,000 rupees, Visa Ultra Cash Back 11,000 (with an issuance fee of 11,000, written as the issue fee), Gold 14,000, Platinum 23,000, Mastercard Optimus 17,000, AMEX Gold 13,500, Signature 30,000 (reduced to 5,000 after spend criteria the schedule doesn't state, not written); a late payment 2,500 rupees flat; a cash advance 1,200 rupees or 3%, whichever is higher; over the limit 2% of the over-limit amount or 1,600, whichever is higher, each month it lasts; a returned cheque or rejected autopay 1,200; foreign transactions 4.5% or 125 rupees, whichever is higher (written as 4.5%). The advance withholding tax on international spending (5% for a filer, 10% for a non-filer), the card maintenance, cash-on-POS and acquiring-bank charges aren't written; the Premier Platinum card, for Premier customers, and the corporate cards aren't. The schedule states no minimum payment or grace period. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: HBL's CreditCard terms and conditions (the version its site links, read 2026-10-30) define the minimum as 5% of the current balance or a sum the bank sets on the statement, written as 5% (its key fact sheet of January to June 2024 added a 500-rupee floor; no later sheet was found, so the floor isn't written). UBL's schedule of charges for July to December 2026 (read again 2026-10-30) sets the minimum monthly payment at 5% of the outstanding balance or 500 rupees, whichever is higher, written as such. Bank Alfalah's credit card summary box for July to December 2026 (read 2026-10-30): 1% of the principal plus any over-limit amount, instalment and all billed mark-up and charges, or 500 rupees, whichever is higher; its AMEX summary box for the same period the same; written on its seven cards as 1% with the interest added and a 500 floor (the charges added aren't modelled).
